gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 cannot take an expansion battery (BLUETTI points to its B80 in Power Bank Mode instead), accepts BLUETTI's Charger 1 alternator charger at 200 W max, and has its 2.2-hour car-socket charge time stated for a 24 V socket only.
standout_why: Compared against Nineteen Lab (cited), Portable Power Rank and Power Station Picks, all opened 2026-11-27. Power Station Picks already says the Elite 30 V2 'comes with AC and car charging cables', and Portable Power Rank already gives its 200 W solar limit and ~10 ms UPS. None of the three mentions expansion batteries, alternator chargers or the voltage behind a car-charge time for any model. The finding that would have scored 2 (solar voltage window per model, so which panels fit) could not be sourced from a maker document I could read.
decides: It does not change the pick. It confirms the Elite 30 V2 as a fixed 288 Wh unit, so a shopper who wants more runtime under $300 should buy a ~500 Wh unit (River 2 Max class) rather than plan to expand. Separately, BLUETTI's page puts ship notices on the two gray colors only (Light Gray Dec 28, Deep Gray early January, the latter over four weeks out) and none on Blush Pink at $289.99; I did not confirm that Blush Pink dispatches immediately, so check before making it the pick.

findings.label: Expansion battery support
findings.value: None. BLUETTI FAQ: "The Elite 30 V2 does not support battery expansion. However, it can be charged using the B80 in Power Bank Mode (Sold Separately)."
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 Portable Power Station | 600W 288Wh (Blush Pink)
findings.note: Maker's US product page FAQ. The B80 acts as an external charging source, not added capacity.

findings.label: Charging sources and limits (maker's charging table)

findings.note: The car-socket time is given for 24 V only; the page gives no 12 V figure. The page gives no solar voltage range, amps or connector, and does not mention Charger 2.

findings.label: What the three rival under-$300 pages cover on compatibility
findings.value: Nineteen Lab: no prices; 10 ms UPS for the Elite 30 V2; nothing on solar voltage, connectors, car charging, expansion or alternator chargers. Portable Power Rank: Elite 30 V2 $299.99 as best overall, solar 'up to 200 W', UPS ~10 ms; solar voltage and connector only for the ALLPOWERS VOLIX P300 and Pecron E300LFP. Power Station Picks: Elite 30 V2 'comes with AC and car charging cables', 10 ms UPS; nothing on expansion or alternator chargers.
findings.source_title: Best Portable Power Stations Under $300 · Portable Power Rank
findings.note: Also read the same day: https://reviews.nineteenlab.dev/best/power-station-under-300/ and https://powerstationpicks.net/best-portable-power-stations-under-300/. None of the three lists the Segway Lumina 500 or the Pecron E500LFP that ChatGPT recommended.
